## Mandated disclosure was supposed to lower prices {#puzzle}

Forty states passed it in six years. Prices rose in half of them.

::: {.aside-note}
Source: Author (2024), Table 2.
:::

## Where search costs are high, disclosure raises prices instead {#claim}

<!-- Clicks: 0 the estimate; 1 the number takes the accent; 2 the reading. -->

::: {.result}
[Estimate]{.label}
[0.29 log points]{.fragment .highlight-accent fragment-index=1} (s.e. 0.04) in the top
search-cost quartile, 0.06 (0.05) elsewhere.
:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment fragment-index=2}
The sign of the policy effect flips with market structure.
:::

## Setting {.section-break}

## The reform hit half the markets in 2018 and none of the others {#data}

- 1,240 markets, 2014 to 2022
- Treatment assigned by a statutory population cutoff
- Prices from weekly scanner data

## Identification {.section-break}

## Identification compares high- and low-search-cost markets before and after {#id-equation}

<!-- Clicks: 0 the fixed effects; 1 the effect of interest; 2 the error and
     the assumption. -->

::: {.eq-stack}
::: {}
$$\log p_{it} = \class{gr}{\alpha_i + \gamma_t}
 \class{hid}{{}+ \class{ac}{\beta\,(\text{Post}_t \times \text{High}_i)}}
 \class{hid}{{}+ \varepsilon_{it}}$$
:::
::: {.eq-layer .fragment fragment-index=1}
$$\log p_{it} = \class{gr}{\alpha_i + \gamma_t}
 {}+ \class{ac}{\beta\,(\text{Post}_t \times \text{High}_i)}
 \class{hid}{{}+ \varepsilon_{it}}$$
:::
::: {.eq-layer .fragment fragment-index=2}
$$\log p_{it} = \class{gr}{\alpha_i + \gamma_t}
 {}+ \class{ac}{\beta\,(\text{Post}_t \times \text{High}_i)}
 {}+ \varepsilon_{it}$$
:::
:::

::: {.eq-notes}
::: {}
$\alpha_i$ absorbs the market and $\gamma_t$ the week.
:::
::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
$\beta$ is the effect of the reform in high-search-cost markets.
:::
:::

::: {.assumption .fragment fragment-index=2}
[Assumption 1.]{.label} Absent the reform, prices in high- and low-search-cost
markets would have moved in parallel.
:::

## Search costs explain the reversal, concentration does not {#mechanism}

<!-- Clicks: 1 to 3 one line each; earlier lines gray. -->

::: {.incremental .dim-past}
- Effect scales with baseline search cost.
- No gradient in concentration.
- Both hold within state and within year.
:::

## Takeaways {#takeaways .closing-slide}

1. Disclosure raises prices by [0.29 log points]{.em} where search costs are high,
   and has no effect elsewhere.
2. Search costs, not concentration, carry the reversal.
3. The claim, restated in the words you want quoted.
